additional_info.subject: ID0392319-DC/Si-D/FI-[Qu2jTM] - Phaseloss during run of with full power CRM:00315002115
additional_info.body:
Dear Markus,
Thank you for reaching out to eMobility Support. My name is
Francisco
, and I will be assisting you with your following query today:
Product
: Sicharge D - Charging Center
Main Asset
:
Ivalo
ChargerID/Serial No.
:
Qu2jTM
Problem Description
: Income_PhaseLoss
Troubleshooting
:
Let's make a timeline of events to make it easier to process:
EVMAC":"02.00.00.00.00.20"
DC1 was successfully established and charging
While it was doing these steps someone tried to charge in DC4 (this one I cannot confirm that it's this specific EVMAC but it should be)
But failed with
"no PLC link"
While DC1 was charging and DC4 was with B PilotState
Tried to charge in DC3
And failed during PreCharge since there was no voltage
While DC1 was charging and DC3 in B State, DC4 was unplugged
And another DC4 was retried
Again with
"no PLC link"
, so I cannot confirm the EVMAC
And DC3 was plugged out
While DC1 was charging and DC4 was B State
Another DC3 test
And this time it worked:
But failed a few seconds later due to Error 67
In between DC4 was plugged out
Another test on DC4 and DC2 simultaneosly
Meanwhile DC3 was unplugged
DC2 is charging with that EVMAC
DC4 fails authentication
While DC1 and DC2 are charging the same EVMAC, another test with DC4:
This one with a different EVMAC =
EVMAC":"00.18.23.96.e8.28
And it's charging
While DC1/2/4 are charging, another test with DC3:
Also successfull
At the end it seems like this
EVMAC":"02.00.00.00.00.20"
, is able to charge in 3 different outlets and they were possibly trying 4. The other EV might be random or not as it's very different from this very specific one.
As you just told me
yesterday there was similar MAC in different location in Finland and ALSO 1 week backwards 3 location in Germany with same MAC.
From my perspective it seems the thing where they took the eActros 600 around Europe and tested many chargers, it can be a similar kind of thing and this EV on DC3 is just a normal passenger EV that they have it besides the truck or battery, or whatever it is.
What do you think?
Regarding the error is very unclear, it all started with the DC2 going to error and then all the others followed. It's a bit difficult to understand what caused it since it just failed in the Converter group which can be one of the following:
Config - CG ID is invalid
Config - CG ID is missing in LCU Converter Group Priorities
Logic - CG is stuck in cooldown state
Logic - SMC connected to CG has Feedback Fault
Logic - EV connection is requested on CGp having less than min converter count
Logic - Priorities evaluated for this CG to be alloted as error during connected SMC feedback fault
Logic - Fast Shutdown check was not done
For future reference, your ticket number is
0392319
, please do refer to this in all further communication regarding this issue.
We thank you for your time and patience in advance.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Francisco de Matos Joaquim

additional_info.subject: ID0392319-DC/Si-D/FI-[Qu2jTM] - Phaseloss during run of with full power CRM:00315002115
additional_info.body:
Hello Markus, good morning.
As we already aligned last week, from the VI team, I got information that there are 2 brands which use the same EVMAC for their trucks, which are Volvo and VW.
It seems that Volvo accidentally did this while VW is supposed to be intended, since there is nothing in the standard that mentions a obligatory unique MAC address.
From the vehicle investigation point of view there is nothing we can do, let's check if there is any fuse blown upstream like the other charger we saw. Otherwise we need to see if there is any problem with the MCCB, please measure the input before and after the MCCB:
If the problem is from before the MCCB, then we have a problem upstream
If the problem is after the MCCB then we might have a damaged MCCB.
I will send this to the RC-FI queue for further troubleshooting, please reach out to me if you need any assistance.
Best regards
Francisco
